correctness.rationale: Every nonempty subsequence occurrence corresponds to a unique nonzero bitmask; OR-ing masks by candidate word detects coverage exactly (OR=all position bits). Restricted-growth canonicalization represents each ternary word up to letter relabeling once. The reviewed C++ direct verifier iterates every canonical word length 1..11 and every nonempty position mask; a second verifier checks every labeled word using greedy prefix/suffix embeddings. Newly written independent integer-encoded C++ full enumeration (distinct storage/encoding) rechecked all 44,292 canonical words, 72,517,166 occurrence masks, the 29,525 canonical length-11 words, the unique exception and both minimizers; Its three distinct symbols have a trivial relabeling stabilizer, so the orbit has precisely 3!=6 labeled words. This is exact finite exhaustive proof of the stated bounded theorem, not a claim for length >=12.
residual_risks: Exhaustion certifies only word lengths <=11; no all-length uniqueness claim.

evidence: Theorem 7.3 builds exponentially many shortest covers over O(log n) symbols; its initial explicit example has four symbols and length 15.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general existence or counting algorithm does not itself give the sharp first ternary ambiguity and classification; the special finite threshold requires full exact enumeration.
